get.description:
Get full document details including file content and test metadata.

Returns the full document record for a document attached to a service
owned by the current seller. File content is always included — callers
decide whether to display it, save to disk, or ignore it.

Supports partial document ID matching (minimum 8 characters).

patch.description:
Skip or unskip a document's test.

Dispatches on the body's ``status`` field:

- ``skip`` — mark the test as skipped (stamps ``skipped_at`` /
  ``skipped_by``). Rejected for ``connectivity_test`` documents (only
  ``code_example`` can be skipped).
- ``pending`` — unskip, and forget the document's recorded runs so the
  next run re-proves it.

The document must:
- Have category ``code_example`` or ``connectivity_test``
- Belong to a service owned by the current seller

get.description:
Full execution details (stdout/stderr/masked env/rendered script) of the
latest recorded run of a document by one of the caller's services.

Selectors narrow the run: none → the newest run; ``interface_id`` (+
optional ``channel``) → that gateway run; ``upstream=true`` (+ optional
``channel``) → the upstream probe. 404 means no such run was recorded;
``expired=true`` means it was, but (some of) its output aged out of
retention — re-run the test to reproduce it. A service's full result set
is at ``GET /seller/services/{id}/test-results``.

Supports partial document ID matching (minimum 8 characters).

post.description:
Execute a code example or connectivity test (seller pre-submission check).

This is the seller's **pre-submission dry-run** tool: it queues a
Celery task that runs the document's script against the platform's
ops_customer API key and records the run in ``document_test_result``
for ``service_id`` — one of the seller's services carrying the document
(documents are shared between a service and its revisions); default: the
newest of them. It does
**not** touch service status or trigger admin review — contrast with
the formal submission flow via
``PATCH /seller/services/{id}`` (status=pending), which queues an
orchestrated test run as part of the review pipeline.

The document must:
- Have category ``code_example`` or ``connectivity_test``
- Belong to a service owned by the current seller
- Not be marked ``test.status == "skip"`` in meta

Test execution uses ``OPS_CUSTOMER_API_KEY`` for gateway access and
injects the gateway URL + key as environment variables into the script.

The run records ``status`` (``success|task_failed|script_failed``),
``error``, ``exit_code`` and ``executed_at``; stdout, stderr, the masked
env and the rendered script are kept in S3 (read them with
``GET /seller/documents/{id}/test-details``). A test passes or fails on
its exit code alone (unitysvc#2490) — assert inside the script and exit
non-zero.

Set ``force=true`` to re-run a document whose test already recorded a
success.

Create or update a promotion by name (idempotent upsert).

If a promotion with the same name exists for this seller, it is updated.
Otherwise, a new promotion is created. This enables CLI-driven workflows

patch.description:
Update a promotion.

Cannot change: code, source, seller_id.

Status transitions are handled here via the ``status`` field in the
request body. Valid transitions:

- ``draft``/``paused`` -> ``active``: activate the promotion. Paused
  promotions go through ``resume_price_rule`` to clear pause metadata;
  draft promotions are updated directly.
- ``active``/``scheduled`` -> ``paused``: pause the promotion via
  ``pause_price_rule`` (customers can no longer redeem).
- Other target states fall through to a plain field update and are
  subject to the underlying CRUD layer's validation.

Non-status fields (name, description, pricing, priority, service_groups)
are updated in a single CRUD call before any status transition runs, so
combining "change pricing and pause" in one call is well-defined.

A partial update that omits ``pricing`` leaves it untouched; one that
supplies it must supply a spec the pricing engine can apply, so a working
promotion cannot be edited into a dead one (#2225).

delete.description:
Delete a promotion.

get.description:
List services owned by the current seller that are deprecated.

Deprecated services are excluded from ``GET /seller/services`` and
from every other browse surface (see #1027). This endpoint exists
only to support the recovery workflow: a seller can find a
deprecated service id and email it to platform support, who has
admin access to flip ``deprecated → active``.

The response is read-only and intentionally minimal — id, names,
provider, and a deprecation timestamp. No filtering or pagination:
a seller's deprecated set is small in practice.

Get complete service data for a service owned by the current seller.

Returns the rolled-up provider + offering + listing records along with
the service's documents (metadata only — fetch file content separately
via GET /seller/documents/{id}) and access interfaces with resolved
gateway base URLs.

Supports partial ID matching on service_id (minimum 8 characters).

delete.description:
Delete a service that has never been active.

A service can only be deleted if:
1. It belongs to the current seller.
2. It has never been active (current status is not active/suspended/
   deprecated). Services that have been active are kept for audit trail.
3. For a platform service: no member service was generated from its member
   template (those belong to other sellers — an admin delete removes them
   together). Its member template family is deleted with it.

When ``dryrun=true``, the deletion is not performed — only the
eligibility check runs and the result is returned in the response
without raising. Use this to drive a proactive "disable delete button"
UX in a dashboard, or to bulk-check a set of services before issuing
the real deletes.

When ``dryrun=false`` (default) and the service cannot be deleted,
a 400 is raised with the reason.

Cleanup of dependent records (access interfaces, enrollments, group
memberships, recurrent requests, revisions) is handled by
``crud_service.delete_service``. The associated content entities
(Provider, Offering, Listing) are content-addressed and may be shared,
so they are not deleted.

Supports partial ID matching on service_id (minimum 8 characters).

patch.description:
Update a service — status, visibility, routing vars, and/or list price.

All fields are optional. Include only the fields you want to change.
Multiple fields can be updated in a single request.

**Status** transitions (seller-allowed):
draft → pending, rejected → pending, rejected → draft,
pending → draft, active → deprecated.

Status changes here are **pure** — no tests are run as a side effect.
In particular ``→ pending`` ("mark pending") simply makes a
draft/rejected/suspended service routable (e.g. so you can test code
examples on-wire); it does **not** run the activation test pipeline.
To submit a service for review (validate + run the gateway tests that
drive ``review`` / ``active`` / ``rejected``), use
``POST /services/{id}/submit``.

**Visibility**: ``public`` / ``unlisted`` / ``private``.
Sellers can only switch between ``public`` and ``unlisted`` here.
``private`` is upload-controlled via
``listing.service_options.default_visibility`` and cannot be changed by
this endpoint.

**Routing vars** and **list price** accept two forms:

- *Full replacement* — a plain dict replaces the entire value::

    {"routing_vars": {"region": "us-east", "count": 42}}
    {"list_price": {"type": "constant", "price": "1.00"}}

- *Partial update* — a dict with ``set`` and/or ``remove`` keys::

    {"routing_vars": {"set": {"count": 43}, "remove": ["region"]}}
    {"list_price": {"set": {"input": "0.40"}, "remove": ["reference"]}}

post.description:
Submit a service for review (``draft`` / ``rejected`` / ``suspended`` →
``pending``) **and** run the activation test pipeline.

This is the testing counterpart to ``PATCH /services/{id}`` with
``status=pending``: the PATCH is a pure status change ("mark pending") with
no side effects, whereas *this* endpoint additionally validates the content
and dispatches the gateway test job that drives the service to
``review`` / ``active`` / ``rejected`` based on the result.

- **Duplicate content** ⇒ ``200`` no-op (idempotent re-submit, so the
  upload-then-submit CI loop in ``unitysvc-services-*`` repos doesn't flap
  red on a "no real changes" merge).
- **Invalid content** ⇒ ``400`` (status set to ``rejected``).
- Otherwise ⇒ status set to ``pending`` and the test pipeline dispatched.

Queue a server-side diagnostic test run on one of the caller's services.

Replaces the local-execution ``usvc_seller services run-tests`` path
(#1105).  Runs every executable document (``connectivity_test`` and
``code_example``) against every active access interface and upstream
channel inside the cluster — the same network environment customers
hit — and falls back to an upstream-mode probe on any channel-level
gateway failure
so the result attributes the fault as ``platform_fault`` vs
``upstream_fault``.  Pass ``category`` to restrict to one document
category (e.g. post-deploy smoke tests that only want
``connectivity_test`` and not the more expensive ``code_example``
runs) without having to look up a document id first.

The service's status is snapshotted and temporarily elevated to
``pending`` if it isn't already in a routable state
(``pending`` / ``review`` / ``active``); the original status is
restored in a ``finally`` block so a worker crash mid-run can't
leave the service permanently elevated.

Each (doc × iface × channel) run is recorded in
``document_test_result`` (read them with ``GET …/test-results``).  The
task return payload duplicates a summary with stdout/stderr truncated
to 16 KB per stream; full streams remain available via
``…/test-results/{run_id}/output``.

Poll via ``GET /v1/seller/tasks/{task_id}``.

Supports partial service ID matching (minimum 8 characters).

``Service.runtime_stats["display"]``, written every 6 hours by
``refresh_service_runtime_stats`` from ``usage_events`` (ops probes
excluded). The window is 7 days for a busy service and longer (up to 90)
for a rarely used one, until it holds enough requests; it is always stated.
Absent below a minimum sample, so a handful of requests never brands a
service. A figure that needs more samples than the window holds (a p95, or
streaming figures for a mostly non-streaming service) is None.

DeprecatedServiceItem.title: DeprecatedServiceItem
DeprecatedServiceItem.description:
GET /seller/services/deprecated — row in the deprecation archive.

Deprecated services are excluded from every browse surface (see
#1027). This minimal shape exists only to
support the recovery workflow: a seller can find a service they
deprecated and email the id to platform support, who has admin
access to flip ``deprecated → active``.

``deprecated_at`` is the service's ``updated_at`` at the time of the
status flip. It can drift if the deprecated row is later edited
(rare), so callers should treat it as "roughly when this was
deprecated", not as an authoritative event time.

DocumentDetailResponse.title: DocumentDetailResponse
DocumentDetailResponse.description:
GET /seller/documents/{id} — full document including file content.

The prior behaviour was file_content=false by default; this response
always includes file_content for predictable codegen.

DocumentExecuteResponse.title: DocumentExecuteResponse
DocumentExecuteResponse.description:
POST /seller/documents/{id}/execute — queues a Celery test run.

This is the seller's pre-submission dry-run tool. It does NOT touch
service status or trigger admin review — contrast with the formal
submission flow via PATCH /seller/services/{id} (set_status=pending).

DocumentTestStatusResponse.title: DocumentTestStatusResponse
DocumentTestStatusResponse.description:
PATCH /seller/documents/{id} — response for skip/unskip.

The status field in the request body selects the operation: skip, or
pending (unskip and forget the recorded runs).

DocumentTestUpdate.title: DocumentTestUpdate
DocumentTestUpdate.description:
Request body for updating document test status.

The ``status`` field drives dispatch:

- ``skip`` — mark the test as skipped (stamps ``skipped_at`` /
  ``skipped_by``). Rejected for ``connectivity_test`` documents (only
  ``code_example`` can be skipped).
- ``pending`` — unskip, and forget the document's recorded runs
  (including earned sticky passes), so the next run re-proves it.

Test results are recorded only by the platform's own runners; a seller
cannot report one.

This endpoint replaces the previously-separate /skip and /unskip routes,
which dispatched to the same backing field via different HTTP verbs.

EnrollmentKeyLease.title: EnrollmentKeyLease
EnrollmentKeyLease.description: A key acting for the enrollment, returned once. Return it when done.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description: Standard 4xx error body produced by FastAPI HTTPException.

GroupOwnerTypeEnum.title: GroupOwnerTypeEnum
GroupOwnerTypeEnum.description: Type of entity that owns a service group.

GroupServiceMember.title: GroupServiceMember
GroupServiceMember.description:
One explicitly-listed member of a manually-curated service group
(unitysvc#1733).

``name`` is the member service's stable name (the same handle rules match on).
``routing_key`` is loaded straight into ``ServiceGroupMembership.routing_key``
— specify it only when the member should be addressed by a key that differs
from its native one; omit it (``None``) to keep the service's own key. Catalog
(rule-based) groups don't use this at all — their members are keyless.

GroupTypeEnum.title: GroupTypeEnum
GroupTypeEnum.description:
Type of service group. Derived from members, not authored.

- ``category``: Parent group for browsing/organization only.
- ``collection``: Services-bearing group that is not routable.
- ``open``: Routable group where keyless requests can fan safely.
- ``keyed``: Routable group where callers must provide a routing key.

ListingStatusEnum.title: ListingStatusEnum
ListingStatusEnum.description:
Status values that sellers can set for listings.

Seller-accessible statuses:
- draft: Work in progress, skipped during publish (won't be sent to backend)
- ready: Complete and ready for admin review/testing
- deprecated: Retired/end of life, no longer offered

Note: Admin-managed workflow statuses (upstream_ready, downstream_ready, in_service)
are set by the backend admin after testing and validation. These are not included in this
enum since sellers cannot set them through the CLI tool.

OfferingStatusEnum.title: OfferingStatusEnum
OfferingStatusEnum.description:
Status values that sellers can set for service offerings.

Seller-accessible statuses:
- draft: Work in progress, skipped during publish
- ready: Complete and ready for admin review
- deprecated: Service is retired/end of life

service_data.description: The platform service's own provider, offering and listing

service_status.description: The platform service's service.json sidecar; its service_id is the platform service's identity (it survives a rename)

member_template.description: The template sellers instantiate to join this platform service

PlatformServiceUpload.title: PlatformServiceUpload
PlatformServiceUpload.description:
A platform service and its member template, published together (#2569).

A platform service is a seller's product: it buys capacity from member
sellers and resells it at a ``/p`` address its listing declares. The member
template is what other sellers instantiate to join it, so it travels in the
same upload and is owned through the platform service.

PriceRuleApplyAtEnum.title: PriceRuleApplyAtEnum
PriceRuleApplyAtEnum.description: When the price rule is applied.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the price rule

source.description: What type of code this rule matches

service_groups.title: Service Groups
service_groups.description: Service group UUIDs this rule applies to. null = all services.

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Higher priority rules are applied first

requires_redemption.title: Requires Redemption
requires_redemption.description: Derived from scope: False when scope.customers is '*' or omitted

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Customer and service targeting (null = all customers, all services)

seller_id.title: Seller Id
seller_id.description: Seller ID for seller-funded promotions (None = platform rule)

PriceRulePublic.title: PriceRulePublic
PriceRulePublic.description: Public schema for PriceRule API responses.

PriceRuleSourceEnum.title: PriceRuleSourceEnum
PriceRuleSourceEnum.description: Source of code matching for price rules.

PriceRuleStatusEnum.title: PriceRuleStatusEnum
PriceRuleStatusEnum.description:
Seller-facing status values for promotions.

The backend may define additional statuses (scheduled, expired,
cancelled) for internal lifecycle management, but sellers only
interact with these three.

name.title: Name
name.description: Seller-scoped rate-limit bucket name. Channels reference this name via rate_limit_refs / ops_rate_limit_refs; all matching refs for the same seller consume the same live gateway bucket.

limit.title: Limit
limit.description: Maximum allowed — in flight for `concurrent`, per window otherwise

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: What is being limited (requests, tokens, concurrent, …)

window.title: Window
window.description: Time window. Omitted for `concurrent`, which is a gauge rather than a counter.

description.title: Description
description.description: Where the number came from, e.g. the provider's published limit for this tier

ProviderAccountRateLimit.title: ProviderAccountRateLimit
ProviderAccountRateLimit.description:
One ceiling the provider grants the SELLER'S ACCOUNT.

This is the only rate limit a seller can state truthfully. Providers scope
their limits to the account that owns the upstream key — OpenAI, Groq and
Anthropic at the org level, Mistral per workspace, Parasail per account —
so the number belongs to the provider record, once, not to each of the
seller's services.

Declaring it per service is not merely coarse, it inverts: a 60 RPM account
ceiling written onto 18 services authorises 1080 RPM against an account
that grants 60. See unitysvc/unitysvc#1937.

What a seller CANNOT state is any individual customer's allowance — that
depends on how many customers are active at request time. The gateway
derives that from this ceiling; nobody authors it.

contact_email.title: Contact Email
contact_email.description: Primary contact email for the provider

status.description: Provider status: draft (skip publish), ready (for review), or deprecated (retired)

documents.title: Documents
documents.description: Documents associated with the provider, keyed by title

rate_limits.title: Rate Limits
rate_limits.description: Ceilings the provider grants the seller's account, shared by every service and customer routed through that credential. Not per service, and not per customer — the gateway derives a customer's share from these.

ProviderData.title: ProviderData
ProviderData.description:
Base data structure for provider information.

This model contains the core fields needed to describe a provider,
without file-specific validation fields. It serves as:

1. The base class for `ProviderV1` in unitysvc-core (with additional
   time_created and services_populator fields for file validation)

2. The data structure imported by unitysvc backend for:
   - API payload validation
   - Database comparison logic in find_and_compare_provider()
   - Publish operations from CLI

Key characteristics:
- Uses string identifiers that match database requirements
- Contains all user-provided data without system-generated IDs
- Does not include permission/audit fields (handled by backend CRUD layer)

ProviderStatusEnum.title: ProviderStatusEnum
ProviderStatusEnum.description:
Status values that sellers can set for providers.

Seller-accessible statuses:
- draft: Work in progress, skipped during publish
- ready: Complete and ready for admin review
- deprecated: Provider is retired/end of life

RoomDelivery.title: RoomDelivery
RoomDelivery.description:
How the room reaches the calling account: ``auto``, ``off`` or a path
for each channel. A new member starts with its account's room defaults
(``room-{notify,email}-as-{host,guest}``).

RoomDeliveryUpdate.title: RoomDeliveryUpdate
RoomDeliveryUpdate.description: Fields left out keep their value.

RoomInvitationCreate.title: RoomInvitationCreate
RoomInvitationCreate.description: A code for others to join the room with (#2819).

external_id.title: External Id
external_id.description: Message id on the external platform

author.title: Author
author.description: Display name of the external person

client_message_id.title: Client Message Id
client_message_id.description: Idempotency key: retries with the same id post once. Defaults to origin.external_id.

RoomPostRequest.title: RoomPostRequest
RoomPostRequest.description: A message in the msg format.

status.title: Status
status.description: The owner's operational status: paused auto-replies with pause_message; readonly lets only the owner and moderators post

retention_seconds.title: Retention Seconds
retention_seconds.description: Effective message retention; null when kept indefinitely

max_retention_seconds.title: Max Retention Seconds
max_retention_seconds.description: The kind's longest retention; null when it has none

RoomSummary.title: RoomSummary
RoomSummary.description: A room the account is in, and the account's place in it.

retention_seconds.title: Retention Seconds
retention_seconds.description: Effective message retention; null when kept indefinitely

max_retention_seconds.title: Max Retention Seconds
max_retention_seconds.description: The kind's longest retention; null when it has none

SecretOwnerTypeEnum.title: SecretOwnerTypeEnum
SecretOwnerTypeEnum.description: Owner type for secrets - determines which entity owns the secret.

name.title: Name
name.description: Secret name (e.g., OPENAI_API_KEY). Must be uppercase letters, digits, and underscores; must start with a letter or underscore.

description.title: Description
description.description: Markdown explaining what this secret is and how to obtain one. Shown to customers who must supply it; never contains a value.

SecretPublic.title: SecretPublic
SecretPublic.description:
Public schema for secret info.

Sensitive rows keep ``value`` omitted/null. Non-sensitive variables include
their decrypted value for authorized callers.

value.title: Value
value.description: Secret value (will be encrypted). May be empty.

sensitive.title: Sensitive
sensitive.description: Whether the value is write-only. Defaults to true on create and preserves the existing type when omitted on update.

description.title: Description
description.description: Markdown explaining how a customer obtains this secret. Omit to leave unchanged; send an empty string to clear.

SecretUpdate.title: SecretUpdate
SecretUpdate.description:
Request body for variable-capable ``PUT /secrets/{name}`` endpoints.

``sensitive`` controls the freshly submitted value. On update, omitting the
field preserves the existing row type; sending it replaces the value and
stores the row with that sensitivity.

SellerEnrollmentPublic.title: SellerEnrollmentPublic
SellerEnrollmentPublic.description:
An enrollment in one of the seller's services, without the customer's
identity. Sensitive parameters are masked.

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name of the promotion (unique per seller)

scope.title: Scope
scope.description: Customer and service targeting. null = all customers, all services (blanket promotion).

priority.title: Priority
priority.description: Higher priority rules are applied first

SellerPromotionCreate.title: SellerPromotionCreate
SellerPromotionCreate.description:
Schema for sellers creating a promotion.

Inherits all fields from PromotionData (unitysvc-core).
The backend auto-sets source=seller_code and seller_id from
the authenticated user, and decomposes scope into internal fields
(code, requires_redemption, service_groups,
PriceRuleServiceTarget) during ingestion.

SellerPromotionUpdate.title: SellerPromotionUpdate
SellerPromotionUpdate.description: Schema for updating a seller promotion.

ServiceDataInput.title: ServiceDataInput
ServiceDataInput.description:
Authored service content for publishing (provider + offering + listing).

Fields are typed against the shared ``unitysvc_core`` models so the
OpenAPI spec carries the full provider/offering/listing schemas, and
generated clients expose typed upload methods instead of ``dict[str, Any]``.
The status sidecar (``ServiceStatus``) is a separate ``service_status``
parameter, not a field here.

ServiceDeleteResponse.title: ServiceDeleteResponse
ServiceDeleteResponse.description:
DELETE /seller/services/{id} — unified response for dryrun and real deletes.

When dryrun=true, only the can_delete/reason fields are meaningful.
When dryrun=false and can_delete=true, the service is deleted and
deleted=true. When dryrun=false and can_delete=false, a 400 is raised.

ServiceDetailResponse.title: ServiceDetailResponse
ServiceDetailResponse.description:
GET /seller/services/{id} — live service record.

The provider / offering / listing fields carry the same typed shapes
the seller used to upload the service (``ProviderData`` /
``ServiceOfferingData`` / ``ServiceListingData`` from
``unitysvc_core.models``), so SDK consumers get autocomplete and
typed access to the nested data without re-defining the schema.

The shape reflects the **live** state of the service, not a snapshot
of the original upload — in particular ``interfaces`` includes all
interfaces available to the caller: listing-native, service-group-derived,
and enrollment-scoped interfaces owned by the caller (ops enrollment for
sellers). Per-customer enrollment interfaces are hidden from sellers.

The embedded ``documents`` carry metadata only; fetch file content
separately via ``GET /seller/documents/{id}``.

ServiceDocumentItem.title: ServiceDocumentItem
ServiceDocumentItem.description:
Document pointer embedded in ``ServiceDetailResponse``.

Includes the fields the seller UI needs to render the documents tab
(split by ``context_type``, show MIME type / visibility, and display
test status via ``meta``). File content still requires
``GET /seller/documents/{id}``.

ServiceEnrollmentStatusEnum.title: ServiceEnrollmentStatusEnum
ServiceEnrollmentStatusEnum.description:
Status of a customer's service enrollment.

Workflow for services requiring parameters (user_parameters_schema exists):

    [not enrolled] → (enroll) → pending → (task completes) → incomplete → (configure) → active
                          │                                                                ↓
                          │                                  paused ← (pause) ←───────────┘
                          │
                          └─→ active  (if required secret already exists)

Workflow for services without parameters:

    [not enrolled] → (enroll) → pending → (task completes) → active
                                                                ↓
                                  paused ← (pause) ←──────────┘

States:
- pending: Celery task is processing (transient, show spinner)
- incomplete: Needs user configuration (required parameters not provided)
- active: Enrolled and fully configured
- paused: Enrolled but temporarily disabled
- cancelled: Enrollment cancelled

Secrets do not affect enrollment status — they are resolved at routing time.

services.title: Services
services.description: Explicit member list for a manually-curated (routable) group. Mutually exclusive with membership_rules; reconciled on upload.

parent_group_name.title: Parent Group Name
parent_group_name.description: Parent group name. Resolved to ancestor_path based on owner context.

parent_group_name.title: Parent Group Name
parent_group_name.description: Parent group name. Resolved to ancestor_path based on owner context.

ServiceKindEnum.title: ServiceKindEnum
ServiceKindEnum.description:
Role of a Service row in the platform-facade model (#1979).

- regular: ordinary seller service (the default).
- platform: platform-owned public facade Service materialized for a
  PlatformService endpoint; customers discover/group/price this row.
- platform_member: private seller service backing a facade; carries
  ``parent_id`` pointing at its facade Service.

``platform_member`` is derivable from ``parent_id`` at write time; it is
stored explicitly so billing/usage queries can distinguish the executed
member identity from the customer-facing facade identity without joins.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name identifier for the service listing (defaults to offering name if not provided)

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description: Human-readable listing name (e.g., 'Premium GPT-4 Access', 'Enterprise AI Services')

status.description: Listing status: draft (skip publish), ready (ready for admin review), or deprecated (retired)

list_price.title: List Price
list_price.description: List price: Listed price for customers per unit of service usage

user_access_interfaces.title: User Access Interfaces
user_access_interfaces.description: User access interfaces for the listing, keyed by name

documents.title: Documents
documents.description: Documents associated with the listing, keyed by title (e.g., service level agreements)

audience.title: Audience
audience.description: Who the service is for and what a buyer must know before enrolling, as short plain-text phrases (e.g. 'US customers only / export restrictions may apply'). Shown before enrollment; informational only, never enforced. At most 8 phrases of 1-120 characters, no URLs or markup.

service_options.title: Service Options
service_options.description: Service-specific options that modify backend behavior. Keys are option names, values are option configurations. The backend decides which options it supports.

ServiceListingData.title: ServiceListingData
ServiceListingData.description:
Base data structure for service listing information.

This model contains the core fields needed to describe a service listing,
without file-specific validation fields. It serves as:

1. The base class for `ListingV1` in unitysvc-core (with additional
   time_created field for file validation)

2. The data structure imported by unitysvc backend for:
   - API payload validation
   - Database comparison logic in find_and_compare_service_listing()
   - Publish operations from CLI

Key characteristics:
- Contains all user-provided data without system-generated IDs
- Does not include permission/audit fields (handled by backend CRUD layer)
- Uses dict types for nested structures to maintain flexibility between
  file definitions and database operations
- Service/provider relationships are determined by file location (SDK mode) or
  by being published together in a single API call (API mode)

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description: Human-readable service name for display (e.g., 'GPT-4 Turbo', 'Claude 3 Opus')

service_type.description: Category for grouping/comparison; omit it when none fits, and describe the service with capabilities and tags

summary.title: Summary
summary.description: One-line marketplace summary (max 200 characters) — shown on collapsed catalog rows and cards. Required everywhere, deliberately: the teaser is part of the offering, not an optional garnish. Renames the vestigial ``tagline`` field (unitysvc/unitysvc#1838).

description.title: Description
description.description: Service description (long-form; the summary carries the teaser)

status.description: Offering status: draft (skip publish), ready (for review), or deprecated (retired)

payout_price.title: Payout Price
payout_price.description: Payout pricing: How to calculate seller payout

upstream_access_config.title: Upstream Access Config
upstream_access_config.description: Upstream access channels, keyed by channel name

exports.title: Exports
exports.description: How other services may use this one (what a customer access request can ask for): {"permissions": {<name>: ["<METHOD> /<path>", ...]}, "options": <JSON Schema object of the options a grant may set>, "options_ui_schema": <rjsf uiSchema>}. Without permissions, the service exports one, invoke, on every route; with permissions, exactly those (invoke only if declared), so a data service declaring read/write is never reached by invoke or service:*. Omitted: invoke only, no options. See unitysvc_core.grants.

documents.title: Documents
documents.description: Documents associated with the service, keyed by title

tags.title: Tags
tags.description: List of tags for the service (arbitrary strings)

ServiceOfferingData.title: ServiceOfferingData
ServiceOfferingData.description:
Base data structure for service offering information.

This model contains the core fields needed to describe a service offering,
without file-specific validation fields. It serves as:

1. The base class for `OfferingV1` in unitysvc-core (with additional
   time_created field for file validation)

2. The data structure imported by unitysvc backend for:
   - API payload validation
   - Database comparison logic in find_and_compare_service_offering()
   - Publish operations from CLI

Key characteristics:
- status maps to database 'status' field
- Contains all user-provided data without system-generated IDs
- Does not include permission/audit fields (handled by backend CRUD layer)
- Provider relationship is determined by file location (SDK mode) or
  by being published together in a single API call (API mode)

ServiceProbeResult.title: ServiceProbeResult
ServiceProbeResult.description:
The daily connectivity probe's latest verdict on a service.

From ``Service.runtime_stats["last_health_check"]``
(``service_health_tasks.probe.stamp_health_check``). Only the verdict: the
per-check ``gateway`` / ``upstream`` records hold request details and error
text that are not for the public page.

``outcome``: ``healthy`` (passed), ``upstream_fault`` (the provider's
service failed the check) or ``platform_fault`` (the platform failed it,
not the provider; #866).

ServicePublic.title: ServicePublic
ServicePublic.description:
Public Service model for API responses.

Note: name is stored on Service; display_name and other decorated fields
are populated from read queries in the API layer.

service_id.title: Service Id
service_id.description: Backend-assigned service id from a previous publish. When present on upload, the request targets the existing service (revise/replace) instead of creating a new one.

revision_of.title: Revision Of
revision_of.description: Set when this record describes a revision: the canonical service id the revision derives from. ``service_id`` is then the revision's own id.

status.title: Status
status.description: Service identity status as resolved by the last ingest.

time_created.title: Time Created
time_created.description: When the service was first created (informational provenance).

template_instance_id.title: Template Instance Id
template_instance_id.description: Set when the service was published from a seller TemplateInstance (the seller-instances flow). Like ``service_id`` it is consumed on the way *in* to declare the operation — with no ``service_id`` it creates a service from the template (the backend pins the form's service_id); with one it updates an existing template-generated service — and echoed on the way *out* so ``service.json`` records the template association. Absent for plain (non-template) services.

ServiceStatus.title: ServiceStatus
ServiceStatus.description:
Backend-assigned service **status / identity sidecar** (the ``service.json``
file) — *not* the authored service data.

A service's ``provider_data`` / ``offering_data`` / ``listing_data`` are the
authored service data; this is the *other*, backend-owned half — the status
record the backend materializes once a service exists. It is the
**round-trip** sidecar: the ingest task returns it, the seller stores it in
``service.json`` beside the spec files, and replays it on the next
upload/revision so the backend can match the upload to the existing service.

Of these fields, ``service_id`` and ``template_instance_id`` are consumed on
the way *in* (they declare which service / which template the publish
targets); the rest are populated on the way *out* as informational status /
provenance for the seller. ``extra="ignore"`` keeps unknown keys from
breaking either direction.

ServiceStatusEnum.title: ServiceStatusEnum
ServiceStatusEnum.description:
Status of a Service (identity layer).

Workflow:
- draft: Not yet submitted for review (default, seller still editing)
- pending: Tests running (transient, after seller publishes)
- review: Tests passed, awaiting admin approval
- active: Approved and operational, accepting requests
- rejected: Admin rejected (seller can revise and republish)
- suspended: Admin suspended due to issues/violations
- deprecated: Service ending

name.title: Name
name.description: URL-friendly slug identifying the template family (e.g. 'openai-compatible-llm'). Sellers bind to the active version of a name; admin-data directory names and the CLI key off it. Unique per (name, version).

version.title: Version
version.description: Template version label (e.g. 'v1'). The .j2 bodies and parameter_schema are frozen per version; a change is a new version. UNIQUE(name, version).

display_name.title: Display Name
display_name.description: Human-readable template name shown in the seller picker.

description.title: Description
description.description: What kind of service this template produces.

service_type.description: Service type every instance of this template produces.

ServiceTemplateCreate.title: ServiceTemplateCreate
ServiceTemplateCreate.description:
Schema for creating/updating a ServiceTemplate (admin upload).

``status`` defaults to ``draft``; the renderer bodies and schemas are
required so the stored row is self-contained.

``id`` is honored on CREATE only (the ``template_id.json`` sidecar
replayed across environments, so a template keeps ONE id on staging and
production — the same convention service ids follow). The upsert key
stays ``(name, version)``: on update the id is ignored.

ServiceTemplateSummariesPublic.title: ServiceTemplateSummariesPublic
ServiceTemplateSummariesPublic.description: List envelope for seller-facing template summaries.

ServiceTemplateSummary.title: ServiceTemplateSummary
ServiceTemplateSummary.description:
Seller-facing read model — the bounded input surface only.

Excludes the Jinja2 bodies and platform ``constants`` (the seller never
sees the rendered offering/listing schema or the platform-fixed context).

ServiceTestResultsResponse.title: ServiceTestResultsResponse
ServiceTestResultsResponse.description:
GET /seller/services/{id}/test-results — a service's test results.

A service is tested on its own documents through its own interfaces; a
platform member on its PLATFORM SERVICE's documents, through the platform
service's ``/p`` address pinned to it (#2622) — then
``platform_service_id`` / ``platform_service_name`` are set. ``passed`` /
``error`` are the admission verdict; ``runs`` are the runs that decide it
(plus a service's upstream probes); ``not_run`` are required runs that
are missing or stale — the same computation the verdict uses. Output for
a run: ``…/test-results/{run_id}/output``.

ServiceTypeEnum.title: ServiceTypeEnum
ServiceTypeEnum.description:
Broad service category — defines the access pattern and protocol.

Optional on an offering: a service that fits none leaves it out, and
describes what it does with capabilities and tags.

AI modalities (vision, tools, rerank, etc.) are tracked via the
`capabilities` list on ServiceOffering, not service_type.

ServiceUpdate.title: ServiceUpdate
ServiceUpdate.description:
Unified request body for updating a service.

All fields are optional — include only the fields you want to change.
Multiple fields can be updated in a single request.

``routing_vars`` and ``price`` accept two forms:

- **Full replacement** — a plain dict replaces the entire value::

    {"routing_vars": {"region": "us-east", "count": 42}}

- **Partial update** — a dict with ``set`` and/or ``remove`` keys::

    {"routing_vars": {"set": {"count": 43}, "remove": ["region"]}}

ServiceUploadResponse.title: ServiceUploadResponse
ServiceUploadResponse.description:
POST /seller/services — response for async upload.

The upload is queued via Celery: ``task_id`` is the Celery task id
(== Idempotency-Key when one was supplied).  Poll the task backend
for the final result.

ServiceVisibilityEnum.title: ServiceVisibilityEnum
ServiceVisibilityEnum.description:
Visibility of a service in the catalog.

- unlisted: Live and routable, not in catalog, accessible via direct link
- public: In catalog, fully discoverable
- private: Live and routable, ops/internal use only

SkippedTestDocument.title: SkippedTestDocument
SkippedTestDocument.description: A test document the seller marked ``skip``.

name.title: Name
name.description: Optional seller label recorded in source metadata.

auto_submit.title: Auto Submit
auto_submit.description: If true, submit the rendered draft service for review immediately.

TemplateInstantiationRender.title: TemplateInstantiationRender
TemplateInstantiationRender.description: Render a platform-owned template without creating a service.

TemplateInstantiationRenderResponse.title: TemplateInstantiationRenderResponse
TemplateInstantiationRenderResponse.description: Fully rendered service content for inspection, without persistence.

TemplateStatusEnum.title: TemplateStatusEnum
TemplateStatusEnum.description:
Lifecycle status of an admin-owned ServiceTemplate.

Invariant: at most one ``active`` version per template ``name`` — the one
sellers bind new forms to. Publishing a new ``active`` version
auto-deprecates the prior active one. Deprecated templates can no longer
generate net-new services, but services already built from them can still
be revised against their pinned version.

TestDetailResponse.title: TestDetailResponse
TestDetailResponse.description:
GET /seller/documents/{id}/test-details — one recorded run's details.

Serves the bulky per-execution fields (stdout/stderr/masked env/rendered
script) of a run recorded in ``document_test_result``, read from S3
(``source="blob"``). ``expired=True`` means the run exists but (some of)
its output has aged out of ``TEST_DETAIL_RETENTION_DAYS`` — re-run the
test to reproduce the details; ``status``/``executed_at`` still describe
the recorded outcome.

TestRun.title: TestRun
TestRun.description:
One recorded run of a test document (#2622): through one of the
service's interfaces (``interface_id``), or an upstream probe
(``interface_id`` null).

TestRunGap.title: TestRunGap
TestRunGap.description:
A run admission requires but does not have: never run
(``reason="missing"``) or, for a platform member, run before the test or
the member changed (``reason="stale"``).

TestRunOutputResponse.title: TestRunOutputResponse
TestRunOutputResponse.description:
GET /seller/services/{id}/test-results/{run_id}/output.

The run's stdout, stderr, rendered script and masked env. ``expired``
means the run is recorded but (some of) its output aged out of
``TEST_DETAIL_RETENTION_DAYS`` — re-run the tests to reproduce it.
